text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland and Yugoslavia signed an agreement on avoiding double taxation, during a visit of Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to Warsaw on Thursday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by five percent in 1997 and by 4.9 percent in 1998, a report by the Organisation for Economic Coperation and Development (OECD) said.

- The Huta Katowice steel mill had a net loss of more than 100 million zlotys last year, more than any forecasts said. The supervisory board has dismissed the plant's president Bogdan Kolomyjski and appointed Jerzy Smedzik, the former board member, to the post.

- Kredyt Bank (KB) in Warsaw has signed a cooperation agreement with the West Ukrainian Commercial Bank in Kiev, KB said. Kredyt Bank together with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Rabobank and Bank Ukraina plan to launch the Kiev International Bank (KIB) this year.
- The listed ComputerLand's results in the first quarter of 1997 were bad due to insufficient cooperation between the firm's subsidiaries, Computerland's president Tomasz Sielicki said.

- The Gdansk municipality, northern Poland, has issued munibonds worth 18.8 million zlotys to finance the purchase of new buses for urban transport. The city will issue bonds worth 48.6 million zlotys by the end of 1997.
- AmerBank has joined a banking consortium, which is to extend a $22 million credit for the Gdynia shipyard.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Foreign trade and distribution firm Net-Trade has proposed its creditors a 50 percent debt write-off and converting the remaining liabilities into shares, Net-Trade president Wojciech Topinski said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Debica tire maker netted 6.3 million zlotys in May on sales of 62.7 million zlotys, the company said.
- PPABank netted 948,300 zlotys in May and had revenues on interests of 6.8 million zlotys, the bank said.
ZYCIE
- Global economic boom forecast for the next two years may boost Polish exports, the cabinet's strategic studies president Zbigniew Kuzmiuk said.
PARKIET

- The listed Tonsil sound system maker will be Japanese Pioneer's main loudspeaker maker in Europe, the Pioneer Electronic Corporation president Seiya Matsumoto said. NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
